answer: A numbered shale slab split open on a knoll above the river reveals a fossil fern across its two faces; holder keeps one half, keeper the other, photographed with the slab number and date. Two verifiers return within 24h, split a second slab from the same seam, and match fossil pattern and slab number; no two split faces fit alike. A moved slab or a duplicate number locks and burns the deposit; 100 fakes need 100 fossil slabs and 100 knoll trips.
